description: Frozen, source-authored calibration inputs for Evidence Contract v3.

cases.question: Which company depends more on cloud/subscription revenue, Microsoft or Apple?
cases.context:
[Source 1] MSFT 10-K, MD&A
Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion.

[Source 2] AAPL 10-K, MD&A
Services net sales were 109,158 million.
cases.answer: Microsoft disclosed Microsoft Cloud revenue of $168.9 billion [Source 1]. Apple disclosed Services net sales of 109,158 million [Source 2]. These differently scoped absolute amounts do not establish which company depends more on cloud or subscription revenue as a share of total revenue in the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: Which company depends more on cloud/subscription revenue, Microsoft or Apple?
cases.context:
[Source 1] MSFT 10-K, MD&A
Cloud revenue was 30% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025.

[Source 2] AAPL 10-K, MD&A
Cloud revenue was 20% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025.
cases.answer: Microsoft's cloud revenue was 30% of total revenue, compared with Apple's 20%, in fiscal year 2025 [Source 1] [Source 2]. Microsoft is higher on this same-period share measure.

cases.question: What are all the major risk factors Microsoft discloses?
cases.context:
[Source 1] MSFT 10-K, Risk Factors
Intense competition creates strategic and competitive risk.

[Source 2] MSFT 10-K, Risk Factors
Trade laws, sanctions, and restrictions may affect the business. Cybersecurity regulation and compliance costs may increase. The company discloses handling of personal data.

[Source 3] MSFT 10-K, Risk Factors
AI development, deployment, and use may cause reputational or competitive harm or liability.

[Source 4] MSFT 10-K, Risk Factors
Outages, data losses, and service disruption create operational risks.

[Source 5] MSFT 10-K, Risk Factors
Evolving legal, regulatory, and litigation requirements create risk.
cases.answer: The supplied excerpts identify these primary risk groups: strategic and competitive risk from intense competition [Source 1]; trade risks from laws, sanctions, and restrictions [Source 2]; cybersecurity risks including regulation and compliance costs [Source 2]; handling of personal data [Source 2]; AI risks involving reputational harm, competitive harm, or liability [Source 3]; operational risks from outages, data losses, and service disruption [Source 4]; and legal, regulatory, and litigation risks from evolving requirements [Source 5].
